motivation: The fixed-cap CPU-normalized study on seeds 4121-4125 is directionally positive but always ran feedback_off before feedback_on and used post-hoc throughput normalization rather than equal CPU stopping budgets.
question: At a predeclared equal cgroup CPU-time budget, does feedback-on produce more independently confirmed distinct NoREC bugs than feedback-off on paired fresh seeds?
primary_outcome: Number of distinct SQLancer++ NoREC discrepancies per paired seed under identical cgroup-v2 usage_usec stopping budgets, after blinded deduplication and independent reproduction.

design.randomization: Within each seed pair, randomize arm order from a recorded seed; use balanced AB/BA blocks across pairs.
design.cpu_budget: Choose a fixed per-arm CPU-second budget using only the completed pilot's resource distribution, then freeze it before any new outcomes. Stop each arm at the same cgroup-v2 usage_usec target; log the final counter and any overshoot.
design.attempt_limits: Keep the existing per-database query cap and maximum databases as safety caps; do not treat hitting a cap before the CPU target as a complete equal-budget run.
design.bug_triage: Export all candidate mismatches without condition/seed labels; canonicalize SQL and database state; have an independent rerun verify each discrepancy and cluster duplicates before unblinding.

hypotheses.null: Feedback-on does not increase distinct independently reproducible bug yield per equal CPU budget.
hypotheses.alternative: Feedback-on increases distinct independently reproducible bug yield per equal CPU budget.

stop_and_interpretation_rules: No optional stopping or seed replacement after outcomes are visible.
A query-pair throughput gain without distinct bug gain is not an effectiveness win.
Report nulls, duplicate reports, unreproducible mismatches, and incomplete CPU-budget runs.
Do not make Paper 3 forecast or Paper 4 utility claims from this experiment.
current_blocker: Implement and validate reliable in-container CPU-budget stopping and blinded mismatch export before preregistering the next seed block.
